corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.1_the_hedging_signature_is_ABSENT_OFFLIN: TWO HALVES, AND ONLY ONE IS MEASURED. OFFLINE, measured on the validation split: the hedging signature is ABSENT -- saturated-row error is LOWER than unsaturated, conditional means reach 88-98% of the boundary on both signs, and the predicted-to-TARGET standard-deviation ratio is 0.952-0.980. The statistics the original reading was taken from could not have shown this either way: cloning.action_error's unconditional median necessarily sits inside the non-saturated group at 44.503% val saturation, and output_std_per_dimension is predictions only, so 'compressed' had no referent. ONLINE: whether dz behaviour caused the closed-loop failure is UNMEASURED and stays unmeasured, because the signs of every closed-loop command are unrecoverable. The prediction in apple_policy_v1.md section 12 and declared risk R5 range over BOTH halves, so the words 'refuted', 'contradicted' and 'did not occur' are NOT USED UNQUALIFIED anywhere; every statement carries 'offline' or 'on the validation split'. Expert saturation: 44.886% TRAIN, 44.503% VAL, reported separately.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.2_the_sign_of_every_TASK_056_command_is_: scripts/evaluate_policy.py computed every stored command statistic from np.abs(...). Zero negative numbers exist anywhere in command_statistics across all 64 attempts. |dz| q50 = 0.0125 is equally consistent with descending slowly, ascending slowly and oscillating about zero; |grasp| q50 = 1.0 is equally consistent with a hand held fully OPEN - which is what the expert does through orient and descend - and one held fully closed. The under-shoot reading in apple_policy_v1_results.md section 16 and task056_handover.md section 5 is therefore UNMEASURED rather than refuted. This is why D1-grasp is the most informative probe here.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.3_both_learned_arms_grasped_and_lifted_t: A2 on seed 45100 and A3 on seed 45006 each reached the scorer's grasp stage, lifted the apple +0.1678 m and +0.1694 m against a 0.05 m gate, and were STILL HOLDING IT, undropped, when the 1000-step cap ended the attempt. Neither reached transport. The 1/16 counts ARE in apple_policy_v1_results.md sections 14 and 16; the lift height, the sustained contact and the undropped state are nowhere in the record; and task056_handover.md gives neither arm's grasp count at all, stating only the controls' 0/16. The compression into the handover removed the run's single most encouraging measurement.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.4_the_near_constant_reading_is_translati: Median across attempts: dx q90/q50 1.00-1.22 and dz 1.01-1.32, versus droll q50 0.179-0.243, q90 0.478-0.498, q99 0.503-0.513 (ratio 2.05-2.67). Stated at that strength and no further: droll's out-of-distribution rate is 5-7% and its q90 sits at the 0.5 configured bound, which is LESS saturation than the expert's measured ~27% at |max|, so this is not roll running away. The observation is that the one dimension with real online variance is rotational, and it is the dimension with the SMALLEST offline error in Table A. shadow_expert_command.consequence_for_D3_declared_before_any_n: A D3 configuration can inject a lift-phase ascent into an attempt whose hand has never closed on anything. A confound on the only gate. shadow_expert_phase is logged per step, and a G-SUB pass whose attempts spent most of their commands past the expert's close phase is REPORTED AS SUCH next to the pass. Reporting requirement, not a threshold.
shadow_expert_command.definition: scripted.apple_collector_policy(sim.task_truth()).action(robot) at indices (6,7,8,9,10,11,13) -- EarlyReleaseOracleManipulationPolicy(opening_ramp=0.08) with palm_x_offset=+0.015 on every phase and transfer_x_shift=-0.035 on phases 4-7, no aim offset and no perturbation, i.e. exactly the policy whose collector__base_action is the BC target on every surviving root -- advanced by advance(result) on every executed step, computed strictly AFTER the controller's act() returns. Implemented as embodied_jepa.policy_diagnostics.ShadowExpert.
shadow_expert_command.it_is_a_HYBRID_reference_after_roughly_s: advance(result) is called on THE POLICY'S executed result, so the expert's phase counter advances on the policy's clock rather than its own progress. A policy that has gone nowhere still drives the reference into descend and then lift. It is 'expert targets on a policy-driven clock' and is named that way wherever used.
shadow_expert_command.it_is_exhausted_after_745_commands: apple_collector_policy's phase table is orient 130, descend 80, close 45, lift 150, transfer 60, release_high 100, lower_open 100, retreat 80 = 745 (= collect_apple_wide.ROOT_MAX_COMMANDS), and action() RAISES 'scripted policy has finished' once done. The harness catches exactly that message and nothing broader. Phase boundaries on the controller's clock: close starts at step 210, lift at 255, transfer at 405, release_high at 465, lower_open at 565, retreat at 665.
shadow_expert_command.its_release_grasp_depends_on_the_EXECUTE: AMENDMENT 1, a hybrid property the frozen text could not state because it named the wrong policy: from release_high (phase index 5) on, the collector commands grasp = max(-1, accepted_grasp - 0.08), where accepted_grasp is the grasp component of the last EXECUTED action. In an unsubstituted or partly substituted attempt that is the controller's grasp, not the expert's own previous command. Declared, not corrected: it is how the collector itself behaved under perturbation.

Val saturation is 44.503%, below half, so that median necessarily sits inside the NON-saturated group and the cell is MATHEMATICALLY INCAPABLE of testing 'large error on the saturated rows'. output_std_per_dimension is PREDICTIONS ONLY -- target std is never computed, so 'compressed' had NO REFERENT. An earlier draft drew a conclusion from both; that conclusion is withdrawn and these conditionals replace it.

Selection scores reproduce: A1 0.011059 < A0 0.013129 < A2 0.017935 < A3 0.023404.

Computed from the 6-dp values in this file, which the protocol's printed Table A now reproduces at the same precision; an earlier revision quoted doc-rounded 0.00673/0.03029 next to a ratio computed from the 6-dp values.
frozen_offline_error_table_A.what: median |predicted - expert| per dimension on the val split, 7723 rows, 15 surviving val roots
frozen_offline_error_table_A.withdrawal_clause_status: DISCHARGED - the re-derivation agreed, so nothing is withdrawn

D1.derivation: Float noise between act()'s single-observation path and the batched training path is <= 1.61e-6 (A2; A0 2.4e-7, A1 8.3e-7, A3 6.0e-7). The smallest input change that must be detectable -- another val root's reset image -- moves the output by at least 3.15e-3 (A1; A2 1.13e-2, A3 6.7e-3); a zeroed image by >= 0.576; the next frame's state by >= 0.0215. 1e-4 sits 62x above the noise and 31x below the smallest such change. Inputs are compared exactly because they are exact in a sound pipeline.
D1.name: D1-pipeline: observation-path equivalence at reset (amendment 1)
D1.population: the 15 surviving val roots, reset coordinates from collect_apple_wide.make_plan; zero commands executed; nothing scored
D1.rule: D1 FAILS for arm X iff on ANY of the 15 val resets: (i) for A1/A2/A3, the closed-loop onboard_rgb frame is not byte-identical to the stored training frame; or (ii) the closed-loop robot_state differs from the stored state by more than 1e-6 in any component, or the state mask differs; or (iii) any of the seven free components of X's act() output differs from X's offline prediction on the stored frame by more than 1e-4. A0 consumes no image, so (i) does not apply to it.

D1_contrast_reported_not_decisional.derivation: the offline error is measured on recorded val frames at arbitrary phase; a reset frame is one specific in-distribution phase, so the claim tested is 'same order', not 'equal'. The per-dimension errors themselves span 4.50x, so a factor below 3 cannot be distinguished from ordinary per-dimension variation while 10x or more is unambiguous. A judgement call fixed before the numbers exist; realized ratios reported per dimension whatever they are.
D1_contrast_reported_not_decisional.rule: passes for arm X iff, for EVERY one of the six arm dimensions, the median across the 16 seeds of |step-zero policy - shadow expert| is <= 3x X's own frozen_offline_error_table_A cell
D1_contrast_reported_not_decisional.status: AMENDMENT 1: demoted from gate to report. Thresholds unchanged (3x Table A, frozen_D1_thresholds_three_times_table_A).

D1_grasp.derived_two_sided_count: seeds where step-zero right_grasp > -0.5, i.e. |g - (-1.0)| > 0.5. Fires on the prior-only predictor (-0.0092), on an inert 0.0 and on a closed +1.0; does not fire on -1.0 or on -0.5. Sound arms on recorded reset frames: max |g+1| = 0.023, 0 fires on val (15) and train (137) for every arm.
D1_grasp.primary_report: the SIGNED step-zero right_grasp value, per arm per seed -- the full 4x16 table of numbers, not a count
D1_grasp.reading: the policy is not commanding the hand open at the one instant where the correct command is known and unambiguous
D1_grasp.reference: the expert's step-zero right_grasp is -1.0 EXACTLY on every reset (scripted.py orient phase), so no threshold is needed
D1_grasp.why_a_count_of_grasp_greater_than_zero_w: ONE-SIDED, and AN INERT POLICY PASSES IT: a head emitting exactly 0.0 scores ZERO sign errors and reads correct while being wrong by a full unit against a reference known exactly. That is the blind-baseline failure apple_policy_v1.md 5.1 was rewritten to remove, and the SECOND threshold in this design with that shape; the first was the original G-SUB.

D2.first_departure_step_definition: AMENDMENT 1 (the frozen text named first_departure_step and never defined it): the first step t at which departure > tau_X on 5 consecutive steps t..t+4, where departure is the median over the six arm dimensions of |controller - shadow expert| and tau_X = 3 x the median of arm X's six Table A arm-dimension cells. Steps after the shadow expert's exhaustion end the search (departure undefined, never zero). No departure found = censored at the attempt's last defined step and counted as that step for the median.

persistence_calibration.why_5: with persistence 1, open-loop A1 departs at a median step 43 (< 50) on its own training-distribution frames, so 'gradual' would be unreachable for a sound arm; with 5, every arm's open-loop median is >= 116 and the prior-only predictor's is 0.

D2.why_stated_this_way: apple_policy_v1.md section 5.3 announced a rule was 'not a gate' and then decided gate outcomes through the missing-values rule (apple_policy_v1_results.md section 15). D2 feeds nothing.

G_SUB.CORRECTION_carried_in_the_open: An earlier draft defended this gate against a demo_replay null of p0=1/3 and quoted 'the one-sided binomial probability of >= 8/16 is 0.189'. 0.189 IS WRONG: P(X>=8|n=16,p=1/3) = 0.126501. 0.189 corresponds to p0 = 0.363344, which nothing here uses. At the correct value the FAMILY-WISE probability across the eight candidates is 0.661077, so under that null the gate would have been near a coin flip rather than the screen it was presented as. The demo_replay null is DROPPED ENTIRELY: it is an open-loop baseline while G-SUB asks whether substitution moves THIS policy.
G_SUB.derivation_of_8_of_16: the midpoint between the pure-policy 1/16 = 6.25% and the 100% ceiling: the effect must be at least half the distance to the ceiling. A MAGNITUDE threshold, not a significance threshold; D is non-gating and no p-value from it is a result.
G_SUB.metric: grasp resets out of 16, per configuration, A2 only
G_SUB.null_defended_against: the PURE POLICY'S OWN RATE, 1/16 (outputs/task056-cohort-d/a2.json). That is the rate substitution must beat for substitution to have done anything, and the only null with a defensible claim to being this experiment's.
G_SUB.precision_note: Stored at full double precision rather than rounded. A consistency test recomputes each from the stated null and the enumerated candidate count; rounding made that test fail at 1e-6 and the fix is more digits, not a looser tolerance.

reference_points_fixed_before_the_run.scripted_oracle: 24/24 pooled on three prior wide cohorts

G_SUB.rule: passes iff at least one of the EIGHT G-SUB CANDIDATE configurations c reaches >= tau_c grasp resets, tau_c = max(8, floor((r_c + 16) / 2)), r_c = max(1, b_c), b_c = the grasp resets of candidate c with the TIME-INDEXED BLIND complement on the same 16 resets (amendment_1 calibration). 'none' and 'full' are CONTROLS and NOT candidates.
G_SUB.threshold_rule_note: AMENDMENT 1. The frozen floor of 8/16 is kept, so no candidate's threshold is lower than before. The binomials are informational: the simulator is deterministic and the blind references are exact counts on these 16 resets, not estimates.

missing_values: AMENDMENT 1 (the frozen value read 'D1 and G-SUB are the only gates', stale against protocol section 5): a quantity that cannot be evaluated counts as failed. This covers D1 (D1-pipeline), D1-grasp's derived count, and G-SUB -- every quantity that decides an outcome. D1-contrast and D2 decide nothing and are excluded by name.
not_done_declared: any model, loss, head or output-parameterisation change
the on-policy-relabeling argument for a follow-up, which is recorded in the results document as a named candidate and deliberately NOT preregistered here

pre_declared_outcomes.P: Clause (a) holds -- clause (a) (amended): D1-pipeline FAILS for A2 or for >= 3 of the 4 arms, OR D1-grasp's derived count (step-zero right_grasp > -0.5) is >= 8/16 for >= 3 of the 4 arms. A locatable pipeline discrepancy. Next: an audit of the observation path from G1Embodiment.observe to ClonedPolicy.act against cloning.py's training path, then a re-measurement. No model change, no retrain.
pre_declared_outcomes.P_over_X_precedence: G-SUB fails AND clause (a) HOLDS BY EITHER DISJUNCT: OUTCOME P TAKES PRECEDENCE AND OUTCOME X DOES NOT FIRE, once. exemption_spent is set to true in the results document, and a re-run after the fix whose G-SUB fails with clause (a) not holding fires the abandonment clause as written.
pre_declared_outcomes.S: Clause (a) does NOT hold (D1-pipeline passes for A2 and for >= 2 of the 4 arms, AND D1-grasp's count is < 8/16 for >= 2 of the 4 arms) and G-SUB passes. The failing channel is named. Next: a new preregistration for a targeted fix, with its own controls. That task may ask for cohort C.
pre_declared_outcomes.V: B1, B2 or B3 fails. The run is void. No arm numbers are reported as results; the defect and the void are recorded.
pre_declared_outcomes.X: G-SUB fails AND clause (a) does NOT hold. The abandonment clause fires. The line stops.
pre_declared_outcomes.X_when_the_exemption_is_already_spent: If exemption_spent is already true and G-SUB fails while clause (a) holds, THE ABANDONMENT CLAUSE FIRES. The exemption is gone; a second failure through a channel that was supposed to have been fixed is the clause case, not an exception to it. Properly the successor protocol outcome to declare, but the entire point of exemption_spent is that this protocol binds its successor, and an unnamed cell is exactly what the B-2 defect was.
pre_declared_outcomes.a_grasp_latched_before_exhaustion_still_: Under the definition of grasp_reset ('a development seed on which the latched score.grasp is true at any point'), termination by shadow_expert_exhausted ends the attempt but does not un-latch a stage already reached.

precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.amended_clause_a: clause (a) (amended): D1-pipeline FAILS for A2 or for >= 3 of the 4 arms, OR D1-grasp's derived count (step-zero right_grasp > -0.5) is >= 8/16 for >= 3 of the 4 arms. The precedence, the once-only bound and exemption_spent are UNCHANGED; D1 now names D1-pipeline. A2 is named because G-SUB is conducted through A2's channel alone.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.exemption_spent_contract: Frozen at false. The results document sets it true the first time the exemption is claimed. ANY SUCCESSOR PROTOCOL MUST CITE THIS FIELD IN ITS OWN GATE SECTION and may not claim the exemption while it reads true. Without a field to flip, 'once' is prose binding a document this protocol cannot reach.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.guards_must_match_the_CONDITION_not_the_: A guard that matches on vocabulary rather than on the condition will pass any mutation fluent enough to reuse the vocabulary. The decision-table guard asserted that Outcome X MENTIONS clause (a) and not that it fires when clause (a) does NOT hold, so an Outcome X rewritten to "G-SUB fails AND clause (a) HOLDS" -- the B-2 defect in the correct vocabulary -- passed the guard built to prevent it. Reproduced, then fixed by asserting polarity, then re-verified by re-running that injection.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.keyed_on_clause_a_not_on_D1_alone: An earlier revision stated the precedence over the D1 disjunct only, so on (D1 passes all four, D1-grasp >= 8/16 for >= 3 arms, G-SUB fails) the success clause and Outcome P said continue while the abandonment clause and Outcome X said stop -- VERBATIM the contradiction the rule was written to remove, one disjunct over. The case is live rather than theoretical: grasp is a separate normalization path and the one dimension with an exactly-known reference, so it is the disjunct most likely to fire alone.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.rule: CLAUSE (a) AS A WHOLE takes precedence -- EITHER DISJUNCT. If either D1 fails for >= 3 of the 4 arms OR D1-grasp's two-sided count is >= 8/16 for >= 3 of the 4 arms, the observation the controller receives is not the one the trainer used. G-SUB's result is then UNINTERPRETABLE RATHER THAN NEGATIVE -- a sweep conducted through a broken channel measures the channel. In that case the abandonment clause does NOT fire; the task reports a pipeline defect, and the line continues for the purpose of fixing it. THIS EXEMPTION IS AVAILABLE EXACTLY ONCE, tracked by exemption_spent; the D1_grasp disjunct is covered because the precedence is keyed on clause (a), not on D1 alone.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.the_defect_it_fixes: An earlier revision had the abandonment clause fire unconditionally on a G-SUB failure while the success clause said the line continues if D1 fails for >=3 arms. On the joint outcome 'D1 fails for >=3 arms AND G-SUB fails' -- plausible, arguably the modal one -- one clause said stop and the other said continue, and the pre-declared outcomes listed both side by side with NO PRECEDENCE. A preregistration whose function is to bind the executing agent left the agent free to pick AFTER SEEING THE NUMBERS.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.the_exemption_is_available_exactly_once: Once the defect is fixed, a re-run whose G-SUB fails with clause (a) not holding fires the clause as written. The exemption is recorded as spent by setting exemption_spent to true in the results document the first time it is claimed, so a second claim is visibly unavailable.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.why_the_once_is_load_bearing: Without it this is an unbounded escape from abandonment, which is worse than the contradiction it replaces.

predecessor.outcome: failed on the development stop rule; 0 full successes over 64 development attempts

probes.D1: D1 (amended) = D1-pipeline, the observation-path equivalence probe: for each of the 15 surviving val roots, reset the simulator to that root's recorded reset exactly as scripts/evaluate_policy.py resets a development seed, take the first observation, and compare it and each arm's act() output against the stored training-path frame and the arm's offline prediction on it. Zero commands are executed. The frozen D1 (step-zero contrast against the shadow expert on the development cohort) is kept as D1-contrast: reported, never decisional.
probes.D1_contrast: reported, not decisional: signed step-zero command vs shadow expert (apple_collector_policy), 4 arms x 16 development seeds, per-dimension median |difference| and its ratio to 3x Table A. Declared before the run: on recorded reset frames all four arms exceed 3x Table A in right_dx (ratios 3.76-5.37 on val, 4.40-5.32 on train).
probes.D1_grasp: the expert's step-zero right_grasp is -1.0 exactly on every reset (apple_collector_policy, orient phase). PRIMARY REPORT: the signed step-zero right_grasp per arm per seed, the full 4x16 table. DERIVED, DECISION-RELEVANT COUNT: seeds where step-zero right_grasp > -0.5 (|g - (-1.0)| > 0.5).
probes.D2: divergence trace, 4 arms x 16 seeds x <=1000 steps, signed per-step logging of both commands plus ||palm-apple||, stage, step index; first_departure_step as defined in gates.D2 (amendment 1)

D2_named_traces.contrast_rule: the lowest-numbered seed of the same arm, chosen by rule rather than inspection so it cannot be picked after the traces are seen

probes.D3: per-dimension expert substitution, A2 only, 10 configurations x 16 seeds: the 8 G-SUB candidates plus the controls 'none' and 'full'
probes.no_dimension_is_privileged: D2 and D3 report all seven dimensions. The protocol does NOT report dz preferentially: the largest online/offline behavioural gap in TASK-056 is in droll, not translation.

authorizations_in_order_neither_implying: merge the preregistration on the reviewer's REPORTED APPROVE
process.reported_verdicts_only: A gated run starts only on the pre-run reviewer's REPORTED verdict, delivered as a message - never on a review file read from disk. The same rule applies to merging.

shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.BLOCKING_DEFECT_THIS_FIXES: An earlier revision keyed the rule on 'D3', and 'none' IS a D3 configuration, so every 'none' attempt would have terminated at ~805 with shadow_expert_exhausted. B2 requires 'none' to reproduce outputs/task056-cohort-d/a2.json, whose sixteen attempts are ALL step_limit at exactly 1000 executed steps. B2 could never have passed, Outcome V would have fired, and THE RUN WOULD HAVE BEEN VOID WITH NO ARM NUMBERS REPORTED. 'full' was never at risk: orient+descend+close = 255 commands, +lift = 405, well inside 805. The second-order hazard is worse: a preregistration that provokes its own violation invites the executing agent to reason its way out of an obviously-unintended void mid-run, which is exactly what the process section's 'stops and reports rather than repairing as a reflex' exists to prevent.
shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.amendment_1_note_on_the_BLOCKING_DEFECT_: '~805' in BLOCKING_DEFECT_THIS_FIXES describes the frozen revision's wrong expert; with the collector the same defect would have terminated every 'none' attempt at 745. The fix (keying on the substitution set) is unaffected.
shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.empty_substitution_set: all of D1 and D2, the 'none' configuration of D3, and B1's three reference baselines scripted_oracle, hold and random. The shadow expert is a RECORDING, not a command source, so its exhaustion cannot affect the robot. It stops being recorded, THE ATTEMPT CONTINUES TO ITS CAP, and the report records shadow_expert_exhausted_at_step. Departure past that step is null, NEVER zero.
shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.non_empty_substitution_set: 'full' and the eight G-SUB candidates. The expert IS part of the commanded action, so at exhaustion (step 745) the attempt TERMINATES with reason shadow_expert_exhausted and counts as a NON-SUCCESS. Not a concession: scripted_oracle IS apple_collector_policy, its budget is 745 commands, and it succeeds inside it on 16/16 of exactly these resets (apple_wide_grasp_closure_results_v3.md) -- AMENDMENT 1 (the frozen text said 805).
shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.reported_for_every_attempt: shadow_expert_exhausted_at_step, so a reader can see how many attempts the rule bound.

success_clause: GOVERNED BY precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB, which ranges over CLAUSE (a) AS A WHOLE. Continues iff EITHER (a) clause (a) (amended): D1-pipeline FAILS for A2 or for >= 3 of the 4 arms, OR D1-grasp's derived count (step-zero right_grasp > -0.5) is >= 8/16 for >= 3 of the 4 arms - follow-up is a pipeline audit and re-measurement, NOT a model change and NOT a retrain; OR (b) G-SUB passes (a candidate reaches its per-candidate threshold), naming the failing channel. If EITHER DISJUNCT of (a) holds AND G-SUB fails, clause (a) applies and the abandonment clause does not fire, ONCE. In both cases the follow-up is a NEW preregistration with its own gates and controls.
what_this_task_is: A DIAGNOSTIC task. It trains nothing, changes no model, and proposes no output-parameterisation change. Its only purpose is to locate the gap between TASK-056's near-perfect open-loop imitation and its closed-loop failure. Its single gate can fire the abandonment clause that apple_policy_v1.md section 7 already preregistered.
